courses.title: The Flux language
courses.summary: The terms a sponsor, a steward, and a practitioner share before a project starts. For the wider group that only needs the language.
modules: Knowledge, a unit, and a comp
The value cycle in one pass
Enterprise debt and velocity
Open text and controlled marks
outcomes: Define knowledge, enterprise debt, velocity, and a value session in the Flux sense.
Point to where a unit lives and name its owner.
Tell the open text of the standard from a controlled mark.
courses.format: Self-paced reading, with a written check at the end.

courses.title: Foundations
courses.summary: How a practitioner turns a fact from outside the organization into an accepted unit. This is the course a Practitioner candidate studies.
modules: The Big Pause, and why it comes first
Frontmatter, type, and scope
The asset register and the debt register
Value sessions and the unit types
What an examiner grades
outcomes: Draft a decision unit with the required frontmatter.
Place a fact on the asset register or the debt register and say why.
State velocity as a number of days, from arrival to an accepted unit.
courses.format: Cohort. Four live sessions and a practical.

courses.title: Steward practice
courses.summary: The organizational steward's instruments: the learner map, both registers, readiness, and the board report the sponsor signs.
modules: What the sponsor signs, and what the steward signs
The learner map
Keeping the asset register and the debt register
Readiness on five axes
The board report
outcomes: Build a learner map that names who takes which course.
Produce a one-page board report from register counts.
State which decisions the steward does not make alone.

courses.title: Master judgment
courses.summary: For people who already practice. The work is a judgment on a fictional project: what to accept, what to leave as debt, and when to supersede.
modules: When a unit stays draft
Supersession and the version log
Readiness without rounding up
Reviewing a register you did not build
The practical
outcomes: Accept or reject a proposed unit and write the reason.
Supersede a unit without dropping the old id.
Defend each readiness score from the registers, including a low one.
courses.format: Mentored practical on a fictional project.

courses.title: Train the trainer
courses.summary: How a licensed trainer teaches the standard without examining the people they taught. Written for consultancies that deploy the practice.
modules: Teaching the terms without a private dialect
A cohort, a comp, and the registry id
The line between training and examination
Observed delivery
What a trainer license does not allow
outcomes: Deliver one Foundations module from the comp, not from a side deck.
Name who examines a cohort, and why it is not the trainer.
State the limit of the license: teaching is allowed, issuing a mark is not.
